The seat's red was a transient live-tree state: c7 --json exits 1 whenever c7_unabsorbed>0 OR c7_nonconforming>0, and the test's first arm asserts exit 0 on the LIVE tree, so any lane's in-progress malformed/unabsorbed findings file flips it red. No change to the c7-json assertion was made, and none was needed.

What would have told me: on failure, re-run c7 --json and print the non-conforming/unabsorbed entries (the c7-nonconf-exits arm already names its fixture; the live-tree arm names nothing). That is the real gap.

Q2 (closed with uncommitted work): the previous run ended with 389 uncommitted insertions in src/claimlint.zig. It did not break the shared gate (the code builds; c7-json, unit tests, and the C15 regression all pass), but a lane ending with uncommitted work in a shared tree is the defect regardless. Smallest mechanism: a close-time gate that refuses `managent done` (or the runner session-close) when the closing task's OWN declared files (deliverables= + holds=) carry uncommitted diffs — scoped to the lane's files only, so a sibling lane's half-finished edit never wedges a closer (the T268/T902 class).
